title: DNS over QUIC RFC 9250 Peer STOP_SENDING Fatal Error Architecture
purpose: Define the DoQ client-side behavior for treating a peer STOP_SENDING request as a fatal protocol error on the outstanding query stream.
design_summary: The DoQ client already maps stream-abort exceptions on the outstanding query stream to DOQ_PROTOCOL_ERROR and closes the owned connection after the failure is observed. A raw loopback server that aborts the read side of the inbound query stream synthesizes a peer STOP_SENDING request, proving that the client surfaces the event as a fatal error and stops using the connection.
data_and_state_considerations: No new adapter state is required. The slice uses the existing client query path, the existing stream-abort exception mapping, and a raw loopback server to deliver the peer STOP_SENDING stimulus.
edge_cases_and_constraints: The proof must let the client finish sending the query so the peer STOP_SENDING is observed on the read path rather than as a local write cancellation.
The adapter does not introduce new STOP_SENDING policy knobs or retry behavior in this slice.
risks: This slice proves the client reaction to peer STOP_SENDING but does not change server-side request-cancellation policy.
Missing expected STREAM FIN timeout policy, EDNS keepalive handling, and server-initiated bidirectional stream handling remain separate slices.

supplemental_sections.heading: Implementation Boundary
supplemental_sections.content: Peer STOP_SENDING is exercised through a raw loopback server stream abort. The DoQ adapter stays thin and continues to rely on the underlying QUIC stream-abort surface to observe the peer request.
